answers.1: Yellow + Green — both are people-oriented, warm and relationship-focused, so they click socially.
answers.2: Red + Blue — both are task-oriented and results-focused (Red drives, Blue secures quality).
answers.3: Red — the dominant, take-charge profile always wants to lead.
answers.4: Blue — precise, careful, methodical and quality-obsessed (a Red streak helps for decisiveness under pressure).
answers.5: Yellow — loves the spotlight, an audience and talking.
answers.6: Blue — systematic, structured filing and detail memory.
answers.7: Blue — needs facts, data and analysis before committing.
answers.8: Blue — punctuality is part of doing things properly (Green is dependable too, but Blue is clock-precise).
answers.9: Red — the goal matters, the rulebook is negotiable.
answers.10: Red — pragmatic and impatient, will try anything that gets results fast.
answers.11: Green — takes it personally, internalises it and remembers it for years (Blue also broods over criticism).
answers.12: Yellow — chaotic desk, but a huge network and a knack for finding things through people.
answers.13: Red — decides quickly and wants control.
answers.15: Red — thrives on challenge, competition and obstacles to crush.
answers.17: All four together (Red + Yellow + Green + Blue) — a balanced team covers drive, ideas, teamwork and accuracy; no single pair is 'best'.
answers.18: Yellow — talks most, and most enthusiastically.
answers.19: Yellow — quick, open and enthusiastic about new ideas (Red grasps them fast too, but filters for usefulness).
answers.20: Red — delegates, gets impatient with the pace, and takes it back (Blue does the same out of perfectionism).
answers.22: Blue — reads and follows every step, including the last one.
answers.23: No single answer — it mirrors your own profile, since people gravitate to those like themselves (statistically Green is the most common overall).
